title: Always Say Less Than Necessary
coreMove: Use verbal scarcity so others project control onto you instead of measuring every thought
sourcePressure: why verbal restraint can create authority and mystery, how overexplaining weakens presence, and where silence becomes suspicious unless another harmless surface carries the disguise.

sourceAnchors.name: Coriolanus
sourceAnchors.detail: lost political aura once speech became brash and uncontrolled
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Coriolanus had distance until his own words dragged him down into ordinary quarrel.

sourceAnchors.name: Louis XIV
sourceAnchors.detail: used sparse speech to keep people unsure where they stood
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Louis XIV made few words feel like a locked door everyone else had to study.

sourceAnchors.name: Andy Warhol
sourceAnchors.detail: gained an aura of depth from sparse, vague replies
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Warhol let blankness do the work talk would have spoiled.
